From cleats to comics: Inside FAU Football’s comic book business

How the Florida Atlantic Football team contributes to a comic book business started by defensive lineman Gabriel Birnbaum.
Categories:
  • Features
  • Football
  • Sports
  • Top Stories
FAU Athletics
FAU football defensive lineman Gabriel Birnbaum surrounded by his comics
Morgan Larkins, Staff Writer • September 24, 2026
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 5:38
Instaread

From selling random items to doing odd-man jobs, junior defensive lineman Gabriel Birnbaum was doing anything he could to make extra money on the side. One day, Birnbaum was cleaning his uncle’s house, and a box of comics changed his sporadic selling into a lucrative business.

Now, Birnbaum is the proud owner of South Florida Collectables, where he mainly sells comic books. Birnbaum also has another job, helping establish the pass rush as a defensive lineman for the Florida Atlantic University football team.

Birnbaum said that he arrived at FAU as a freshman in 2024 and “didn’t realize you don’t start immediately as a freshman.” So, he decided to find something else to do outside of football.

“I just felt like such a lack of purpose, being here,” Birnbaum said. “I felt this, and it [selling comic books] really gave me a sense of belonging. I didn’t need anyone else. This was just me, and it’s something I love doing.”

Selling comic books led Birnbaum to his mentor, Mordecai Bock, who helped Birnbaum get started in selling comic books. They met at a Whole Foods parking lot every single day after selling comic books.

“Eventually, he ended up hiring me,” Birnbaum said. “Hiring is a loose term, but he ended up recruiting me to sell books for him. In doing this, I learned more about the comics, I learned more about their value, and I learned more how to buy and track, and understand the business.”

Four months after working for Bock, Birnbaum branched off to start something himself. This became South Florida Collectables, and is where Birnbaum really started to grow his business and make more money.

“I ended up creating an account on a site called Whatnot,” Birnbaum said. “So, that’s [selling directly to consumers] about 60% of what I would say our business is. I prefer to sell to wholesalers that are then selling to end consumers. Traveling is a huge part of it”

Traveling is one of the most important aspects of the business. Birnbaum says that he has to “travel quite frequently, anywhere around the country just to buy, sell, trade, meet with people, and just keep everything running smoothly.”

According to Birnbaum, South Florida Collectables has become the largest-selling comic book account [on Whatnot] in the country.

However, Birnbaum doesn’t think much of the accomplishment.

“It’s more of like, how can I stay here and keep people happy?” Birnbaum said. “Customer retention is the biggest part of this business, so [if] you can’t retain your customers, it doesn’t matter how many followers you have.”

Birnbaum highlights great service as the key to retention. “If something’s ever wrong with the book, I let them keep it, and I refund them in full,” Birnbaum said. “You’re transparent, you’re honest, and you let people know why you’re doing what you’re doing.”

With the growth South Florida Collectables has had, Birnbaum was able to hire two different teams and obtain a 4000 square foot office in Deerfield Beach. The two teams are separated into sellers and streamers.

The sellers deliver the goods to various locations and sell directly to consumers. Streamers go live online to showcase the different comic books people can buy.

These two teams are filled with other FAU football players. South Florida Collectables became a team endeavor.

“We were always hanging out, so it was like ‘why not just pick up on it and learn what he’s doing?’” defensive tackle Wilky Denaud said.

While most might think there isn’t time to play football and sell comic books, both Birnbaum and Denaud do not find it too challenging. “It’s not really hard because we manage our time well,” Denaud said. “We still have enough time to get sleep, and it’s not taking away from our actual football time.

Working with fellow teammates who can be called their best friends makes the job fun for everyone. “You don’t want to be at something you don’t enjoy or love,” Denaud said. “So being able to deal with people that you hang out with and that you can call your best friends, I think that’s what makes it fun.”

Denaud provided a story about when Birnbaum brought comic books to the locker room and gave them out. “A lot of guys have never seen comic books really in person, so it was kind of cool,” Denaud said.

The streamers have a different role on staff. FAU long snapper Blake Thomas is one of the streamers for South Florida Collectables, and he says that he is able to sell comic books on Whatnot in an auction style. Thomas showcases the comic book, explains what it is, and then lets the bidding war begin. The highest bidder gets the comic when the time ends.

During one live stream, Thomas sold a comic book for $10,000. That was the largest amount Thomas ever sold on a live stream.

“It’s crazy,” Thomas said. “You have a $10,000 comic book in your hands, you’re watching all these people pay that much money for it. You’re like, ‘holy cow!’”

Birnbaum claims that the highest amount of money he received for a single comic book was $235,000. Comic books, like most things, become more valuable with age, cultural impact, and how many are left in the world. So, it’s no surprise that South Florida Collectables have been so successful in the industry, making “roughly $85,000” a month according to Birnbaum.

Although they still prioritize winning football games on Saturdays, this business showcases another side of these athletes; a side that highlights the players beyond their abilities on the field.

Morgan Larkins is a Staff Writer for the University Press. For more information on this and other stories, email him at mlarkins2023@fau.edu.
